common.searchHint: Type at least 2 characters — IPs, hostnames, MACs, switches, devices…

empty.title: Nothing here yet
empty.description: Once you add data it will show up in this list.

validation.invalidCidr: Enter a valid IPv4 CIDR, e.g. 10.0.30.0/24.
validation.invalidMac: Enter a valid MAC address, e.g. aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.
validation.vlanIdRange: VLAN ID must be between 1 and 4094.

errorCodes.SUBNET_OVERLAP: This CIDR overlaps an existing subnet.
errorCodes.DUPLICATE_CODE: This code is already in use.
errorCodes.VLAN_ID_OUT_OF_RANGE: VLAN ID must be between 1 and 4094.
errorCodes.DUPLICATE_PORT: A port with this number already exists on this switch.
errorCodes.DUPLICATE_LINK: A link between these two ports already exists.
errorCodes.INVALID_LINK: A port cannot link to itself.
errorCodes.RATE_LIMITED: Too many requests — please slow down.

errors.unauthorized: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.
errors.forbidden: You don't have permission to access this resource.

errors.notFoundBody: The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved.
errors.forbiddenBody: Your account doesn't have permission to view this page.

unused.title: Unused
unused.help: No IPs recorded — reclaim opportunity or undocumented inventory.
unused.empty: Every subnet has at least one IP.

site.label: Site
site.empty: No sites yet — create one to start tracking inventory.

help.code: Short identifier (e.g. PAR-DC1). Letters, numbers, dashes and underscores only — used as a prefix everywhere in exports and IPAM.
Short room code (e.g. MDF-01, R-101). Must be unique within the site.

vlan.label: VLAN
vlan.subtitle: VLANs and their colours.
vlan.empty: No VLANs yet — create one to assign to subnets and switch ports.

help.vlanId: VLAN tag, between 1 and 4094. Must be unique. IDs 1, 1002–1005 are usually reserved on Cisco gear.
help.color: Display color for VLAN badges in the UI. No impact on the network — purely cosmetic.

subnet.label: Subnet
subnet.subtitle: Your IP ranges and how full they are.
subnet.empty: No subnets yet — create one to start planning your IP space.
subnet.treeEmpty: No subnets in this scope — create one to get started.

tree.rootDropHint: Drop here to detach a subnet from its parent.
tree.attached: Subnet attached to its new parent.
tree.detached: Subnet detached — now at the root.

subnet.nextFreeNone: No free address left in this subnet.
subnet.tooLargeTitle: Block too large for per-address view
subnet.tooLargeBody: {cidr} contains more than 4096 addresses. NetForge can't render each IP individually, but the fill rate above stays accurate and every higher-level operation still works.

tooLargeHint.splitChildren: Split this block into smaller subnets (/22 or tighter) — each gets its full grid view.
tooLargeHint.useExport: Export the full list to CSV for one-off audits.
tooLargeHint.useImport: Bulk-register IPs via the CSV importer — it writes rows directly without enumerating the address space.

bulk.title: Reserve or release an IP range
bulk.help: Pick a contiguous range inside {cidr}. Network and broadcast addresses are skipped automatically. Capped at 512 addresses per call.
bulk.statusHelp: Status applied to every newly-created or overwritten row.
bulk.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional — copied onto every created IP.
bulk.overwriteHelp: Without this, addresses that already have a row are skipped. Turn on to mass-flip their status in place.

help.cidr: CIDR notation (e.g. 10.0.30.0/24). The prefix length (/24) sets how many addresses the range covers. Immutable once created.
help.gateway: Default gateway IPv4 for this subnet. Often the first usable address (e.g. .1). Leave empty if there's no gateway.
help.vlan: VLAN this subnet sits on. Leave empty for an untagged subnet.
help.site: Physical location this subnet belongs to. Used for filtering and reporting.
help.vrf: Routing scope. Leave Global unless you reuse the same IP range in another isolated context (multi-tenant, prod vs dev).
help.parent: Optional: file this subnet under a larger one for hierarchical IPAM. Only shows subnets in the same VRF.
help.dhcp: Marks part of the range as a DHCP pool. NetForge tags these addresses as DHCP and excludes them from manual assignment.
help.dhcpRange: First and last IP of the DHCP pool. Both must belong to this subnet.

subnet.pageHelp: Each card shows fill rate, VLAN and gateway. Use the search to filter by CIDR, description, gateway or VLAN. The tree view groups subnets by parent.

help.address: IPv4 address to assign. Must belong to this subnet and not already be in use. Immutable after creation.
help.status: Reserved = held but inactive (no live device). Assigned = active device. DHCP = address came from the DHCP pool.
help.hostname: DNS name or internal label (e.g. srv-app-01). Optional but very helpful to find the IP later.
help.mac: MAC of the device using this IP. Accepted formats: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff, aabb.ccdd.eeff (Cisco).
help.device: Optional link to a device in the inventory. Lets you jump from the IP to its full record.

device.label: Device
device.subtitle: Everything that isn't a switch.
device.eolHint: Vendor end-of-support date — the advisor will surface devices approaching EOL.

help.type: Device category. Used for filtering, dashboard stats and the topology icons.
help.assetTag: Internal code from your inventory or CMDB (e.g. NF-001234). Optional but handy for cross-referencing.
help.warranty: Vendor warranty expiration date. Helps plan replacements before support runs out.
help.eol: Vendor end-of-support date. The advisor flags devices approaching EOL as a risk.

device.pageHelp: Catalogue every device that uses an IP — servers, printers, phones, access points, cameras, UPS. Switches live on their own page.

switch.label: Switch
switch.subtitle: Switches, their ports and links.
switch.empty: No switches yet — create one to auto-generate its ports.
switch.portCountImmutable: The port count cannot be changed once the switch is created.
switch.snmpCommunityHint: Stored as-is in the database. Only visible to administrators.
switch.eolHint: Vendor end-of-support date — the advisor will surface switches approaching EOL.

help.name: Short unique identifier (e.g. sw-core-01). Used as the anchor in exports, the topology and link endpoints.
help.managementIp: Management IPv4 used for SSH, SNMP or telemetry. Must be reachable from the NetForge server.
help.rackPosition: U-position in the rack (e.g. U22 or 1-3 for a multi-U chassis). Helps physical inventory.
help.portCount: Total number of physical ports. NetForge auto-creates the matching port rows. Cannot be changed after creation.
help.snmpCommunity: SNMPv2c read-only community string. Stored as-is. Admin-visible only.
help.firmware: Currently running firmware version (e.g. 17.09.04). Helps track security patches and feature levels.
help.assetTag: Internal code from your inventory or CMDB (e.g. NF-001234). Optional but handy for cross-referencing.
help.warranty: Vendor warranty expiration date. Helps plan replacements before support runs out.
help.eol: Vendor end-of-support date. The advisor flags switches approaching EOL as a risk.

switch.pageHelp: Every managed switch. Click one to see its ports, links, rack view and connected devices.

help.label: Short label (e.g. uplink-core). Helps spot the port's role at a glance — appears in lists and the topology.
help.mode: Access = single VLAN (one end device). Trunk = several tagged VLANs (switch-to-switch uplink). Hybrid = both. Disabled = administratively shut.
help.nativeVlan: Untagged VLAN on this port. In access mode it's the device's VLAN; in trunk it's the VLAN used for untagged frames.
help.taggedVlans: Extra (tagged) VLANs carried by this port. Mostly relevant in trunk and hybrid modes — managed via the dedicated endpoints, separate from the main Save.
help.adminStatus: Desired port state. Down = port has been administratively shut.
help.connectedDevice: Physical device on the other end (e.g. a server). Optional — leave empty for switch-to-switch links, which are described as Links instead.

audit.subtitle: Who changed what, and when.
audit.help: Every write is logged with the author, timestamp, origin IP and full field-level diff. Kept indefinitely — use this to investigate "who changed what, and when".

compare.title: Snapshot diff
compare.subtitle: What changed between two moments in time.
compare.help: Pick a start and end date, then click Run diff. The page lists every entity that was created, updated, or deleted in that window — based on the audit log.
compare.noChangesDescription: Try widening the time window or removing the entity filter.
compare.pickDescription: Choose a start and end time, then click Run diff.
compare.helpFrom: Start of the window. Date and time in your local timezone — converted to UTC before sending.
compare.helpEntity: Restrict the comparison to a single entity type. Leave on All for an overview across the whole inventory.
compare.helpRun: Walks the audit log between the two dates and lists every entity that was created, updated, deleted or briefly created-then-deleted (transient).

webhooks.subtitle: Notify your own systems when inventory changes.

help.section: Webhooks let an external system (Slack bridge, ticketing tool, custom script) react in real time to changes in your inventory. Each delivery is signed so the receiver can verify it really came from NetForge.
help.url: The full HTTPS URL that should receive the POST. Test with services like webhook.site if you're unsure.
help.events: Which changes to send. Use * for every event, or filter with patterns like port.* (all port changes) or site.create.
help.secret: A long random string the receiver uses to verify the signature in the X-Netforge-Signature header. Shown only once — store it safely.
help.test: Sends a synthetic event so you can confirm the receiver is reachable before relying on real changes.

webhooks.eventsHint: Comma-separated. Use * for everything, port.* for one type, or port.create for a specific one.
webhooks.secretTitle: Copy your signing secret now — it will never be shown again.
webhooks.secretHint: Use it on the receiver side to verify each delivery.
webhooks.confirmDeleteMessage: The receiver will stop getting events immediately. Past delivery history is also removed.

errors.eventsRequired: Provide at least one event pattern.

delivery.emptyHint: Use the Test button to send a synthetic event.

empty.title: No webhooks
empty.description: Add one to notify external systems when your inventory changes.

vrf.label: VRF
vrf.subtitle: Group subnets that share the same routing space.

help.section: A VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) is a separate routing world. Most installations don't need them — leave subnets in the default Global scope. Create a VRF only when you have to reuse the same IP range in two isolated contexts (e.g. two tenants, prod vs dev).
help.rd: Optional identifier used in BGP/MPLS setups, format "AS:nn" like "65000:42". Leave blank if you don't run BGP.

vrf.rdHint: Leave blank if you're not running BGP.
vrf.confirmDeleteMessage: Subnets still assigned to this VRF will block the delete — clear them first.

empty.title: No VRFs
empty.description: Add one only if you need to reuse the same IP range in two isolated contexts.

apiTokens.subtitle: Personal keys to call the API from a script.

help.section: API tokens let an external script or CI job call NetForge as you. They inherit your permissions, so treat them like a password — don't share them, and revoke any you stop using.
help.expiry: Pick a date when the token should stop working. Leave empty for a token that never expires (you can always revoke it manually).

apiTokens.nameHint: A short label to help you recognise the token later.
apiTokens.expiresAtHint: Leave blank to never expire (you can revoke manually).
apiTokens.expiryInPast: Expiry must be in the future.
apiTokens.copyFailed: Could not access the clipboard — copy the token manually.
apiTokens.plaintextTitle: Copy your token now — it will never be shown again.
apiTokens.plaintextHint: Store it in a secret manager. If you lose it, you'll have to generate a new one.
apiTokens.confirmRevokeMessage: Any script using this token loses access immediately. This action cannot be undone.

empty.title: No tokens
empty.description: Your personal access tokens will appear here.

topology.subtitle: Visual map of your switches and how they're cabled.
topology.selectPrompt: Click a switch or a link in the graph to see its details here.

empty.title: No topology to display
empty.description: Create switches and inter-switch links to see them appear here.

topology.help: Each node is a switch, each edge is an inter-switch link. Click an element to see its details on the right. Use the layout dropdown to try different arrangements when the graph gets crowded.

help.section: Physical cable metadata: part number, length, install and test dates. Optional — fill in only if you keep cable records.
help.length: Cable length in meters. Useful when diagnosing attenuation on long runs (especially copper > 100m or single-mode > 10km).
help.installedOn: Date the cable was put in. Helps estimate cable age when troubleshooting old runs.
help.lastTestedOn: Date of the last test (Fluke certification, light meter, etc.).

link.endpointsImmutableHint: Link endpoints are not editable. To move a link, delete it and recreate it.
link.deleteConfirm: Delete this link? This cannot be undone.

help.endpoints: Pick the two ports on each side of the link. Both must be free (a port can only belong to one link at a time). Endpoints are immutable after creation.
help.type: Copper = UTP/RJ45. Fiber = SFP / SFP+ / QSFP. DAC = Twinax direct attach. Virtual = logical link with no physical medium (LAG member, VRF stitching).
help.speed: Negotiated rate in megabits per second (1000 = 1 Gbps, 10000 = 10 Gbps, 100000 = 100 Gbps). Match what the ports actually negotiated.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.subtitle: Speed-up navigation. Most shortcuts use a leader key (g) followed by a letter.

import.subtitle: Load data in bulk from CSV files.
import.help: Tip: always start with a dry-run — it validates the file without changing anything. Once the dry-run is clean, re-run without the dry-run option to actually import.
import.entityHint: One file per entity, in the order shown below.
import.filePrompt: Drop a .csv file here, or click to pick one
import.dryRunHint: Recommended for the first pass — the database is rolled back even if everything parses cleanly.
import.helpDryRun: When ticked, NetForge parses and validates every row but rolls back the transaction at the end. Untick to actually write.
import.helpEntity: Pick the entity this CSV describes. The header row must match the columns shown in the template — download it if unsure.
import.helpExportTemplate: Downloads the entity as a CSV with exactly the column names the importer expects. The easiest way to start a new file.
import.helpDownloadAll: ZIP archive containing one CSV per entity — a logical backup of the whole inventory you can re-import as-is.
import.helpMapping: Headers don't match? The AI assistant proposes a mapping from your column names to NetForge fields, so you don't have to rename them by hand.
import.exportTemplateHint: Exports the entity as a CSV with the exact column names the importer expects.
import.downloadAllHint: Exports every entity as CSV in a single ZIP archive — logical backup compatible with the bulk import.
import.orderHint: Dependencies between entities — import in this order on a fresh install.

bulk.title: Import multiple files at once
bulk.subtitle: Drop all your CSVs (or a .zip) — file type is detected from the headers.
bulk.dropHint: Multiple files accepted in one shot — up to 50 files, 50 MiB total.
bulk.dryRunHint: Every file is validated together in the same transaction — nothing is written.
bulk.helpDetect: Each CSV is routed to its entity based on the header row (sites, devices, switches…).
bulk.helpOrder: Files are applied in the right order (sites → rooms → vlans → … → links).
bulk.helpTransaction: Everything runs in a single transaction: any error rolls the whole batch back.
bulk.helpZip: A .zip works too — its CSVs are unpacked and imported on the fly.

report.title: Bulk import report
report.successDryRun: {count} row(s) across {files} file(s) pass validation. Re-run without dry-run to apply.
report.partial: {ok} of {total} rows would apply — fix the listed errors and re-run.

report.title: Last import report
report.successDryRun: All {count} rows pass validation. Re-run without dry-run to apply.
report.partial: {ok} of {total} rows would apply — fix the listed errors and re-run.

errors.tooLarge: File exceeds the 10 MiB upload limit.
errors.tooManyFiles: Limit reached: at most {max} files in one batch.

suggestLinks.title: AI link suggestions
suggestLinks.heading: Find missing links
suggestLinks.description: The AI looks at switch names, port labels and notes to propose topology links that aren't recorded yet. You stay in control: accept or reject each suggestion.
suggestLinks.lastRun: Last scan: {persisted} suggestion(s) kept out of {raw} returned · {latency} ms
suggestLinks.emptyDescription: Run a scan and the AI will propose links based on your current inventory.

ai.acceptedToast: Link created from the AI suggestion.
ai.scanDoneToast: {persisted} new suggestion(s) added out of {raw} returned.

askView.title: Ask AI
askView.subtitle: Ask questions about your inventory in plain English.
askView.placeholder: Ask a question (e.g. how many free ports does SW-CORE-01 have?)
askView.emptyDescription: The assistant reads your live inventory. A few examples to get started:
askView.example1: Which switches have no recorded links?
askView.example2: How many free IPs are left in subnet 10.0.30.0/24?
askView.example3: List the VLANs used on SW-CORE-01.
askView.example4: Which ports are in trunk mode in room R-101?
askView.disabledHint: The AI assistant is disabled. Enable it in Settings → AI to ask questions.
askView.incompleteAnswer: (Answer interrupted — the model stopped before finishing.)
askView.liteContextHint: Sends only identifiers (names, IDs) to the AI. Faster and cheaper, but it won't see descriptions, notes, MACs or vendor info. Turn it off when your question is about that kind of content.
askView.help: The assistant reads your live inventory to answer. Your questions and the data sent are tracked in Settings → AI usage. Don't include credentials or external secrets in your prompts.

advisor.streakTooltip: This finding has appeared in {n} consecutive runs — a fix or an explicit acknowledgement is overdue.
advisor.subtitle: Automated review of your infrastructure.
advisor.emptyDescription: Run the advisor and the AI will review your infrastructure and list its recommendations.
advisor.cleanDescription: The advisor returned nothing on its last run. Re-run periodically to stay up to date.
advisor.help: The AI scans your inventory looking for single points of failure, capacity overruns, security weaknesses, segmentation gaps and naming inconsistencies. Each finding suggests a fix.

integrity.help: Deterministic, AI-free checks: orphaned references, broken constraints, contradictory states. Pure database queries — no provider call, no cost.

drafts.title: Drafted actions
drafts.subtitle: Describe what you want — the AI prepares it for you to review.
drafts.composerPlaceholder: Create a VLAN 50 named IoT on site PAR…
drafts.safetyHint: Drafts are only prepared — nothing runs without an explicit click.
drafts.emptyDescription: Type a request above to prepare your first draft.
drafts.help: The AI turns your prompt into a structured draft action (create VLAN, subnet, site or room). Nothing runs until you click Apply — you stay in control.

schedules.title: Scheduled runs
schedules.description: Periodic advisor / link scan, with optional webhook on new findings.

csvMapping.title: CSV mapping assistant
csvMapping.description: Paste the first lines of your CSV — the AI proposes a column mapping.
csvMapping.emptyDescription: The assistant reads the headers + a few rows to propose a reliable mapping.
csvMapping.pendingNotice: AI mapping queued — applied on the next import.

settings.title: AI assistant
settings.description: Three providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini. Configured via the .env file.
settings.testDescription: Sends a minimal ping to the provider to verify the API key and model before a real scan.
settings.envHint: Update your .env file then restart the backend. Only the key matching AI_PROVIDER is required.

help.section: Central provider configuration. Every AI feature (advisor, drafts, Ask AI, link suggestions, CSV mapping) uses this. If it's disabled, the buttons that need it stay hidden.
help.test: Sends a one-token completion to the provider — confirms the API key, model and network path before a real scan.

usage.title: AI usage
usage.description: Calls, tokens, estimated cost and latency over the window.
usage.emptyTitle: No AI calls in this window
usage.emptyDescription: Run the advisor or ask the AI a question to start populating this dashboard.
usage.disclaimer: Cost derived from 2026-05 public list rates (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google). Real billing may differ (cache, batch, region).
